pencereler.0-5: In a storm on Lake Huron, a freighter's hull cracked across the deck. The
pencereler.5-12: ship broke in two, and everyone but one sailor died. The survivor spent a freezing night on a raft.
pencereler.12-20: The stern kept sailing under its own power after the bow fell away. Investigators blamed the steel. In cold water, it had
pencereler.20-30: become brittle. Its sister ship had cracked in the same storm. Older lake freighters were inspected and reinforced afterward.

segmentler.metin: The Daniel J. Morrell broke in two on Lake Huron.
It took only a storm loading a hull built of brittle steel.
So how could a storm loading a hull built of brittle steel do this?
The answer is hull fracture in cold water, attributed to brittle steel that lost toughness in low temperatures — and it is why older lake freighters were reinforced or inspected for brittle steel.
